limitations: Fresh cohort from the same public generator, not independent-source validation
24 trajectories, one viscosity, one split; seeds measure training randomness only
Mean projection does not guarantee energy dissipation, stability, or accuracy
Numerical references can drift in mean; reference error is not invariant drift
Only received ranges and the complete local subset were checksum-verified

report_origin.omitted: Per-saved-time arrays from evaluations only; all six runs, scalar metrics, cohort identities and acquisition receipt retained.

interpretation: Mean-preserving models held RMS rollout mean drift near 1e-7 for all three seeds.
Field rollout RMSE improved for seeds 0 and 1 but worsened for seed 2; seed 2 failed to beat persistence in both variants.
One-step field RMSE worsened for projected seeds 0 and 1. Preserving one invariant is not general predictive accuracy or stability.
Fresh trajectories and initial-field hashes are disjoint from the earlier cohort, but come from the same public file and generator.
This ten-epoch, three-seed, four-test-trajectory comparison does not establish a general benchmark ranking.
